question: Which of the following is NOT the aim to establish the Directive Principles of State Policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Political democracy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (राज्य की नीति के निदेशक तत्व) are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution and aim to establish a social and economic democracy and a welfare state.

• Political democracy is secured through the Fundamental Rights (Part III) and the framework of elections and equality — it is NOT the aim of the DPSPs.

• The DPSPs seek social democracy, economic democracy and a welfare state, so 'Political democracy' is the exception here.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The DPSPs are borrowed from the Irish Constitution and are non-justiciable (not enforceable in a court of law).

• They act as instructions/guidelines to the State while framing laws and policies.

NOTE

• Welfare state (Option 1): A key goal of DPSPs — securing a social order for the welfare of the people (Article 38).

• Economic democracy (Option 2): An aim of DPSPs — equitable distribution of resources and reducing inequalities (Articles 38, 39).

• Social democracy (Option 3): An aim of DPSPs — establishing justice: social, economic and political.

question: In March 2024, at India's first National Creators Awards, who won the 'Best Creator for Social Change' award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaya Kishori.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At India's first National Creators Awards (राष्ट्रीय रचनाकार पुरस्कार) held in March 2024, Jaya Kishori won the 'Best Creator for Social Change' award.

• The awards were presented by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.

• Jaya Kishori is a well-known motivational speaker and spiritual/devotional storyteller.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The National Creators Award recognised 23 winners across categories to honour excellence in digital content creation.

• Categories included Best Storyteller, Disruptor of the Year, Cultural Ambassador of the Year, etc.

NOTE

• Kamiya Jani (Option 1): A travel content creator (Curly Tales) who won the 'Best Creator in Travel category' award.

• RJ Raunac (Option 2): A radio jockey and content creator, not the winner of this category.

• Pankti Pandey (Option 4): A content creator, but not the winner of the Best Creator for Social Change award.

question: In October 2024, who has been appointed as the Chief of the Indian Coast Guard?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paramesh Sivamani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2024, S. Paramesh (Paramesh Sivamani) took charge as the Director General of the Indian Coast Guard (भारतीय तटरक्षक बल के महानिदेशक).

• He is the 25th Director General of the Indian Coast Guard.

• The Indian Coast Guard is an armed force that protects India's maritime interests and enforces maritime law.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Indian Coast Guard was established on 18 August 1978 and functions under the Ministry of Defence.

• Its motto is 'Vayam Rakshamah' (We Protect).

NOTE

• Ambarish Kenghe (Option 1): Not associated with the appointment as Chief of the Indian Coast Guard.

• Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya (Option 2): Not the Director General of the Indian Coast Guard in this context.

• Neeraj Parakh (Option 4): Not the person appointed as Chief of the Indian Coast Guard.

question: What is the full form of PM-AJAY, seen in news in May 2025?
option_1: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana
option_2: Pradhan Mantri Awas Jan Aadhar Yojna
option_3: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Jan Abhiyan Yojna
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PM-AJAY stands for Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (प्रधानमंत्री अनुसूचित जाति अभ्युदय योजना).

• It is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for the welfare of Scheduled Castes.

• The scheme aims at reducing poverty and improving socio-economic development of SC communities.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• PM-AJAY was formed by merging three schemes: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY), Special Central Assistance to SCSP, and the Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana.

• It focuses on development of SC-dominated villages, income-generating schemes and construction of hostels.

NOTE

• Pradhan Mantri Awas Jan Aadhar Yojna (Option 2): Not an official scheme name; a fabricated distractor.

• Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Jan Abhiyan Yojna (Option 3): Not the correct expansion of PM-AJAY.

• PM Ann-Jal Aarthik Yojna (Option 4): Not a real scheme corresponding to the abbreviation PM-AJAY.

question: As of July 2025, women in India represent only ______ of the STEM workforce, limiting women's access to career opportunities offered by the STEM sector.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 27%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2025, women in India represent only about 27% of the STEM workforce (STEM कार्यबल).

• STEM stands for Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics.

• Despite high female enrolment in STEM education, their representation in the STEM workforce remains low at around 27%.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India has one of the highest shares of women graduating in STEM fields, yet workforce participation lags due to social and structural barriers.

• Improving women's participation in STEM is a key focus for inclusive economic growth.

NOTE

• 43% (Option 1): An overstated figure; does not match the reported STEM workforce share for women.

• 13% (Option 2): Too low; not the figure cited for women in the Indian STEM workforce.

• 6% (Option 4): A very low distractor figure, not the correct value.

question: Who administers and regulates the NPS Vatsalya scheme launched in September 2024?
option_2: Securities and Exchange Board of India
option_3: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The NPS Vatsalya scheme is administered and regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (पेंशन निधि नियामक और विकास प्राधिकरण - PFRDA).

• It was launched in September 2024 as a savings-cum-pension scheme for minors/children.

• Parents/guardians can open and contribute to an account on behalf of a minor, which converts to a regular NPS account on attaining 18 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme was launched by Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

• PFRDA was established in 2013 (statutory under the PFRDA Act, 2013) to regulate the National Pension System.

NOTE

• Reserve Bank of India (Option 1): India's central bank regulating banks and monetary policy, not the NPS.

• Securities and Exchange Board of India (Option 2): The regulator of securities/stock markets, not pension schemes.

• Ministry of Education (Option 4): Handles education policy, not pension regulation.

question: In Global University Employability Ranking 2025, which was the highest ranked Indian university?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IIT Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Global University Employability Ranking 2025, IIT Delhi (आई.आई.टी. दिल्ली) was the highest ranked Indian university.

• The ranking is published by Times Higher Education (THE) and assesses graduate employability as perceived by recruiters.

• IIT Delhi led among the Indian institutions featured in the list.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• MIT (USA) topped the Global Employability Rankings 2025.

• Multiple Indian institutions, including IITs and IISc, featured in the overall list.

NOTE

• Indian Institute of Science (Option 2): A leading research institute in Bengaluru, but not the top-ranked Indian institution in this employability list.

• IIT Bombay (Option 3): A premier IIT, but ranked below IIT Delhi in this employability ranking.

• IIT Kharagpur (Option 4): The oldest IIT, but not the highest-ranked Indian university here.

question: Tulika Maan is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Judo.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tulika Maan is an Indian Judo (जूडो) player.

• She competes in the +78 kg (heavyweight) category.

• She won a silver medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Judo is a martial art and combat sport that originated in Japan, founded by Jigoro Kano in 1882.

• Judo has been a part of the Olympic Games since 1964 (Tokyo).

NOTE

• Athletics (Option 2): Track and field events; not the sport of Tulika Maan.

• Weightlifting (Option 3): A strength sport; not associated with Tulika Maan.

• Badminton (Option 4): A racket sport; not the sport of Tulika Maan.

question: As of June 2025, which of the following city has surpassed Mumbai to become the India's leopard capital?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengaluru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of June 2025, Bengaluru (बेंगलुरु) surpassed Mumbai to become India's 'leopard capital' (तेंदुआ राजधानी) among metro cities.

• A year-long camera-trap survey recorded around 80-85 leopards in and around the city (notably the Bannerghatta landscape).

• This gave Bengaluru the highest leopard count among Indian metros, ahead of Mumbai.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Mumbai's leopards are mainly concentrated in and around Sanjay Gandhi National Park.

• Bengaluru's leopard population is centred around Bannerghatta National Park on the city's outskirts.

NOTE

• Chennai (Option 1): Capital of Tamil Nadu; not declared the leopard capital.

• Bhopal (Option 3): Capital of Madhya Pradesh; known for tigers in the vicinity but not the leopard capital among metros here.

• Hyderabad (Option 4): Capital of Telangana; not the city that surpassed Mumbai in leopard numbers.

question: The Darbhanga gayaki of Dhrupad, a classical form of Indian music, is associated with which Indian state/UT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Darbhanga gayaki (दरभंगा गायकी) of Dhrupad, a classical form of Indian music, is associated with Bihar (बिहार).

• Darbhanga is a city/region in Bihar that lends its name to this gharana (style) of Dhrupad singing.

• Dhrupad is one of the oldest surviving styles of Hindustani classical music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The main gharanas/styles of Dhrupad include the Darbhanga, Dagar, Bettiah and Talwandi gharanas.

• Dhrupad is traditionally sung with a tanpura and pakhawaj accompaniment.

NOTE

• Haryana (Option 2): A northern state; not associated with the Darbhanga gayaki of Dhrupad.

• Gujarat (Option 3): A western state; not linked to this Dhrupad style.

• Jammu and Kashmir (Option 4): A Union Territory; not associated with the Darbhanga gayaki.

question: Which of the following novels is the first in a trilogy written by R.K. Narayan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami and Friends.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Swami and Friends (स्वामी एंड फ्रेंड्स) is the first novel in a trilogy written by R.K. Narayan, published in 1935.

• It is set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi.

• The trilogy continues with The Bachelor of Arts (1937) and The English Teacher (1945).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• R.K. Narayan was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award and the Padma Vibhushan.

• His other famous works include The Guide and Malgudi Days.

NOTE

• The Scream (Option 1): Not a novel by R.K. Narayan (The Scream is famously a painting by Edvard Munch).

• The Namesake (Option 2): A novel by Jhumpa Lahiri, not R.K. Narayan.

• The Hungry Tide (Option 4): A novel by Amitav Ghosh, not part of R.K. Narayan's trilogy.

question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the 'Doongri Festival' of Himachal Pradesh?
option_1: It is celebrated in honour of Hidimba Devi (wife of Bhima).
option_2: It is dedicated to the Goddess of wealth.
option_3: It marks the beginning of the Tibetan year.
option_4: It is celebrated in honour of Lord Shiva.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is celebrated in honour of Hidimba Devi (wife of Bhima).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Doongri Festival (डूंगरी महोत्सव) of Himachal Pradesh is celebrated in honour of Hidimba Devi, the wife of Bhima (of the Mahabharata).

• It is observed at the Hidimba Devi Temple in Manali (Kullu district).

• The festival typically takes place in the month of May and features traditional music, dance and local culture.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Hidimba Devi is worshipped as a local deity in the Kullu-Manali region.

• The Hidimba Devi Temple (Dhungri Temple) was built in 1553 and is famous for its pagoda-style architecture.

NOTE

• It is dedicated to the Goddess of wealth (Option 2): Incorrect; the festival honours Hidimba Devi, not a wealth deity.

• It marks the beginning of the Tibetan year (Option 3): Incorrect; that describes Losar, not the Doongri Festival.

• It is celebrated in honour of Lord Shiva (Option 4): Incorrect; the festival is associated with Hidimba Devi, not Lord Shiva.

question: The Victoria Memorial built between 1906 and 1921 is located in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Victoria Memorial (विक्टोरिया मेमोरियल), built between 1906 and 1921, is located in Kolkata (कोलकाता), West Bengal.

• It was built in memory of Queen Victoria and is made of white Makrana marble.

• It was designed by architect William Emerson in the Indo-Saracenic style.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The foundation stone was laid by the Prince of Wales (later King George V) in 1906.

• It today functions as a museum under the Ministry of Culture and is set within large gardens.

NOTE

• Delhi (Option 1): The national capital; home to India Gate and Red Fort, but not the Victoria Memorial.

• Chennai (Option 3): Capital of Tamil Nadu; not the location of the Victoria Memorial.

• Shimla (Option 4): Capital of Himachal Pradesh; not where the Victoria Memorial stands.

question: 'Sattriya Nritya' is the classical dance of which of the following Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sattriya Nritya (सत्रिया नृत्य) is the classical dance form of Assam (असम).

• It was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardeva.

• It was traditionally performed in Sattras (monasteries) as a part of devotion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sattriya was recognised as a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

• It is one of the eight classical dance forms of India.

NOTE

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Ghoomar and Kalbelia, not Sattriya.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): The home of the classical dance Bharatanatyam, not Sattriya.

• Odisha (Option 4): The home of the classical dance Odissi, not Sattriya.

question: What is SpaDeX, launched by ISRO in December 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A docking experiment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• SpaDeX (Space Docking Experiment - अंतरिक्ष डॉकिंग प्रयोग) was launched by ISRO in December 2024.

• It was a mission to demonstrate in-space docking technology between two small spacecraft.

• It made India the fourth country (after USA, Russia and China) to demonstrate space docking capability.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• SpaDeX was launched aboard the PSLV-C60 rocket from Sriharikota.

• The mission used two spacecraft named Chaser (SDX01) and Target (SDX02).

• Docking technology is crucial for future missions like the Bharatiya Antariksh Station and Chandrayaan-4.

NOTE

• A lunar lander (Option 1): Refers to Moon-landing missions like Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander, not SpaDeX.

• A solar observation mission (Option 2): Describes Aditya-L1, ISRO's solar mission, not SpaDeX.

• A navigation satellite (Option 3): Refers to the NavIC/IRNSS series, not SpaDeX.

question: In February 2025, National Institute of Ocean Technology has been entrusted with the ambitious task of designing and developing the 4th Generation deep-ocean human scientific submersible named ______ as part of the Samudrayan Project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Matsya-6000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The deep-ocean human scientific submersible being developed under the Samudrayan Project is named Matsya-6000 (मत्स्य-6000).

• It is designed by the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai.

• It is designed to carry three humans to a depth of about 6,000 metres in the ocean.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Samudrayan Mission is a part of India's larger Deep Ocean Mission under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

• It aims to explore deep-sea resources and biodiversity.

NOTE

• Samudra-5000 (Option 2): Not the name of the Samudrayan submersible; a distractor.

• Manimekhala-6000 (Option 3): Not an actual submersible name in this project.

• Shankha-5000 (Option 4): Not the name of India's deep-ocean submersible.

question:
Which of the following is known as the Paper tax in India?
I. Wealth tax
II. Goods and Services tax
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, Wealth tax (संपत्ति कर) is known as the 'Paper tax' (कागजी कर).

• It is called a paper tax because it yielded very low revenue relative to the cost and effort of collecting it — it existed largely on paper.

• Due to its negligible revenue and high administrative cost, wealth tax was abolished in 2015.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1 (Only I).

Additional Information

• Wealth tax was levied on the net wealth of individuals, HUFs and companies under the Wealth Tax Act, 1957.

• It was replaced by an additional surcharge on the super-rich (high-income earners) from the 2015-16 budget.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect; GST is a major revenue source and is not called a paper tax.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect; GST is not a paper tax, so both cannot be correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect; wealth tax (I) is indeed the paper tax.

question: Which of the following relates to those expenses incurred for the normal functioning of the government departments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue expenditure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Revenue expenditure (राजस्व व्यय) relates to expenses incurred for the normal functioning of government departments and services.

• It does not create any asset or reduce any liability of the government.

• Examples include salaries, pensions, interest payments, subsidies and administrative costs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Capital expenditure creates assets (e.g., building roads, bridges) or reduces liabilities.

• Revenue expenditure is recurring in nature, whereas capital expenditure is generally non-recurring.

NOTE

• Capital expenditure (Option 2): Spending that creates assets or reduces liabilities, not routine functioning costs.

• Revenue receipt (Option 3): Income of the government (like taxes) that neither creates a liability nor reduces assets — a receipt, not an expenditure.

• Capital receipt (Option 4): Receipts that create liabilities or reduce assets (like borrowings) — a receipt, not an expenditure.

question: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board was initially constituted in India under the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prime Minister's Office.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB - विदेशी निवेश संवर्धन बोर्ड) was initially constituted under the Prime Minister's Office (प्रधान मंत्री कार्यालय) in the early 1990s.

• It was set up to consider and recommend Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) proposals that required government approval.

• It was later moved under the Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The FIPB was abolished in 2017, and its functions were transferred to the respective administrative ministries/departments.

• Most FDI now comes through the automatic route, simplifying investment approvals.

NOTE

• Parliament of India (Option 2): The legislative body; it did not initially house the FIPB.

• Finance Commission (Option 3): A constitutional body for Centre-State fiscal relations, unrelated to the FIPB.

• President of India (Option 4): The head of state; the FIPB was not constituted under the President.

question: The Reserve Bank had first introduced the Banking Ombudsman Scheme in ______ to provide expeditious and inexpensive forum to bank customers for resolution of their complaints relating to deficiency in banking services.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Reserve Bank of India first introduced the Banking Ombudsman Scheme (बैंकिंग लोकपाल योजना) in 1995.

• It provides an expeditious and inexpensive forum for bank customers to resolve complaints relating to deficiency in banking services.

• It was introduced under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme has been revised over the years; in 2021, the RBI integrated it into the Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS).

• The RB-IOS follows a 'One Nation One Ombudsman' approach.

NOTE

• 1996 (Option 2): Not the year the Banking Ombudsman Scheme was first introduced.

• 1991 (Option 3): The year of economic liberalisation, but not of the Banking Ombudsman Scheme.

• 1992 (Option 4): Not the year the scheme was introduced.

question:
Which type of bill cannot originate in the State Legislative Council of an Indian state?
I. Money Bill
II. Ordinary Bill
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Money Bill (धन विधेयक) cannot originate in the State Legislative Council (राज्य विधान परिषद).

• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).

• An Ordinary Bill, however, can originate in either House (Assembly or Council) of a bicameral state legislature.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1 (Only I).

Additional Information

• The Legislative Council can only delay a Money Bill by up to 14 days; it cannot reject or amend it.

• Similarly, at the Centre, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect; Ordinary Bills can originate in the Legislative Council.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect; only the Money Bill (I) is restricted, not Ordinary Bills.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect; the Money Bill (I) indeed cannot originate in the Council.

question: The Konkan Railway connects ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Roha and Mangalore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Konkan Railway (कोंकण रेलवे) connects Roha (in Maharashtra) and Mangalore (in Karnataka).

• It runs along the western coast of India through the states of Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka.

• The route is about 741 km long and passes through the scenic Konkan region.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Konkan Railway is famous for its numerous tunnels and bridges, including the Panval Nadi viaduct (tallest) and the Karbude tunnel.

• It was a major engineering achievement, spearheaded by E. Sreedharan.

NOTE

• Kolkata and Cuttack (Option 2): These eastern cities are not connected by the Konkan Railway.

• Cuttack and Hyderabad (Option 3): Cities in eastern/southern India, not on the Konkan route.

• Kochi and Chennai (Option 4): South Indian cities, not connected by the Konkan Railway.

question: In India, the second five year plan ended in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1961.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, the Second Five Year Plan (दूसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना) ran from 1956 to 1961, so it ended in 1961.

• It was based on the Mahalanobis model and emphasised rapid industrialisation, especially heavy industries.

• It laid the foundation for public-sector steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture.

• The Planning Commission (which framed these plans) was set up in 1950 and replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

NOTE

• 1950 (Option 1): The year the Planning Commission was established, before the plans began.

• 1955 (Option 2): Falls within the First Five Year Plan period, not the end of the Second Plan.

• 1972 (Option 4): Corresponds to the Fourth Five Year Plan period, not the Second Plan.

question: As per MOSPI report of 2024, sex ratio of India by 2036 will be ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 952.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the MOSPI (Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation) report of 2024, India's sex ratio (लिंगानुपात) is projected to improve to 952 women per 1,000 men by 2036.

• This was reported in the 'Women and Men in India 2024' publication.

• The improvement signals a positive trend toward gender balance in the population.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's population is projected to reach around 152.2 crore by 2036.

• The proportion of females in the total population is expected to rise slightly, reflecting a progressive demographic shift.

NOTE

• 972 (Option 2): Not the projected sex ratio figure for 2036 as per the MOSPI report.

• 932 (Option 3): A lower figure; not the projected value for 2036.

• 982 (Option 4): An overstated figure; not the projected 2036 sex ratio.

question: In which direction does the electrical impulse travel in a nerve cell of an animal after being created?
option_1: From the dendrite to the cell body, then along the axon
option_2: From the axon to the dendrite
option_3: From the cell body to the axon
option_4: From the synapse to the muscle cells
solution_text:
The correct answer is From the dendrite to the cell body, then along the axon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a nerve cell (neuron), the electrical impulse (विद्युत आवेग) travels from the dendrite to the cell body, and then along the axon.

• Dendrites receive the impulse/signal, the cell body (soma) processes it, and the axon carries it away to the next cell.

• This unidirectional flow ensures signals move from the receiving end toward the transmitting end.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the end of the axon, the impulse reaches the synapse, where neurotransmitters carry the signal to the next neuron or a muscle cell.

• The axon is often covered by a myelin sheath, which speeds up impulse conduction.

NOTE

• From the axon to the dendrite (Option 2): The reverse of the actual direction; impulses do not normally travel this way within a neuron.

• From the cell body to the axon (Option 3): Incomplete/partial; it omits the initial dendrite-to-cell-body stage of the impulse path.

• From the synapse to the muscle cells (Option 4): Describes signal transmission at a neuromuscular junction, not the direction of the impulse within the nerve cell.
